> I am building Astra Companion, a 2 wheeled self-balancing AI desktop robot featuring a custom 2-layer PCB, a 3D-printed chassis, and an animated OLED eye display. The robot connects to WiFi to act as a physical desktop assistant, processing voice commands via cloud AI APIs. Using an onboard gyroscope and motor drivers, it actively balances upright on two wheels, turning to face me, nodding, and displaying expressive eye animations when we interact. Hardware & Tools Microcontroller: ESP32-S3 (Dual-Core, WiFi/Bluetooth, I2S hardware support) Motion & Sensing:MPU6050 6-Axis Gyroscope/Accelerometer, 2× N20 Metal Gear Motors, DRV8833 Dual H-Bridge Motor Driver Audio & Display: INMP441 I2S Digital Microphone, MAX98357A I2S Audio Amplifier with a 2W Speaker, 0.96" I2C OLED Display Design & Fabrication: Designed in EasyEDA/KiCad, 3D modeled in Fusion 360/Onshape, and manufactured through JLCPCB via the Hack Club On-Board grant. How It Works & Architecture Dual-Core Execution: Core 0 runs a real-time PID balancing loop (updating 100 times per second) to keep the robot upright. Core 1 handles wifi connectivity, audio sampling, and API requests in the background so the balancing loop never freezes. Voice & AI Pipeline: The INMP441 microphone streams audio to a cloud AI model via HTTP API calls. The returned response triggers speech through the speaker, updates the OLED display with pixel-art eye expressions (happy, thinking, surprised), and initiates subtle motor gestures like nodding or turning. Goals & Learning Outcomes Through this project, I am transitioning from basic breadboard electronics to full custom hardware development. I am learning: 1. PCB Design &amp; Fabrication: Schematic capture, copper trace routing, power filtering, and surface-mount soldering. 2. 3D CAD Modeling:  Designing a multi-part mechanical chassis with integrated motor mounts, battery compartments, and screen bezels. 3. Embedded Systems & Control Theory: Implementing PID feedback loops, dual-core task allocation, I2C/I2S communication protocols, and integrating cloud APIs on embedded hardware.
